items.q: Which statement best distinguishes a claim from a verified fact?
a: A claim is true when it sounds precise.
A claim is what a source states; verification requires supporting evidence.
Any statement in an archive is automatically verified.
items.why: Attribution alone does not verify the underlying event.

items.q: A catalogue lists a document that you have not opened. What can you confirm?
a: The listed record exists in the catalogue.
Every statement made about the document is true.
The document proves the claim.
items.why: Catalogue metadata and the content of the document are distinct.

items.q: What does LIMIT indicate in the Bottino Method?
a: A statement that must be deleted.
A point that current evidence cannot establish.
A fact confirmed by two websites.

items.q: Three sites repeat the same press release. How many independent confirmations have been established?
a: Three
One at most; independence has not been established
Two
items.why: Repetition of one source is not independent corroboration.

items.q: Two documents give incompatible dates. What should you do first?
a: Choose the earlier date.
Hide the discrepancy.
Document both accounts and investigate provenance.
items.why: Conflicts must remain visible until resolved.

items.q: AI supplies an archival reference that exists, but its document has not been examined. What is verified?
a: The document proves the AI claim.
The catalogue reference exists.
The AI summary is accurate.
items.why: A real reference does not verify a proposed interpretation.

items.q: A municipal resolution of 6 April authorises work. Which conclusion is directly supported?
a: Work began on 6 April.
Work was authorised in the terms stated by the resolution on 6 April.
Work ended on 6 April.
items.why: Authorisation is not the same as commencement.

items.q: A newspaper dated 7 April says work began yesterday; a later unsourced webpage says 5 April. What is the best treatment?
a: Report the conflicting accounts and leave the start date unresolved.
Accept 5 April.
Accept 6 April without qualification.
items.why: The sources conflict on the event date.

items.q: What makes a research dossier auditable?
a: A polished conclusion without references.
Only an AI-generated summary.
Sources, provenance, classifications, checks, unresolved conflicts and limits.
items.why: An audit must reconstruct the evidence and reasoning.

items.q: When can a source's statement be presented as verified fact?
a: When repeated often.
When supported by sufficient verifiable evidence in context.
When an AI confidently confirms it.
items.why: Confidence and repetition are not verification.

items.q: How should an unexamined archive record suggested by AI be classified?
a: Its existence may be confirmed in the catalogue, but its contents remain unverified.
As definitive proof.
As automatically false.
items.why: Distinguish catalogue metadata from document content.
